scams.name: George Town Tourist-Hypnosis (Pukau) Robbery Ring
scams.description: Penang's most-press-documented 2025 violent-financial tourist crime is the pukau (hypnosis) distraction-robbery ring working George Town, Gurney Drive, Pulau Tikus and Jalan Penang. NST 'Iranians remanded over tourist hypnosis scam' (nst.com.my article 1254749, Aug 3 2025) reported that five Iranians including a married couple were remanded after three theft reports between July 30 and Aug 1, with robberies of foreign tourists in Persiaran Gurney and Pulau Tikus at 7.45pm–9pm. NST 'Hypnosis scam: Five Iranians charged with theft and drug possession' (nst.com.my article 1273039, Sep 2025) confirmed charges, and FMT 'Raid on Penang bungalows busts scam ring preying on Japanese victims' (freemalaysiatoday.com, Nov 28 2025) plus Star 'Cops nab 18 foreign nationals in Penang scam call centre raid' (thestar.com.my, Nov 28 2025) show the broader syndicate footprint. Community reports confirm the pukau tradition. The 2025 tactics: (a) a well-dressed foreigner approaches a solo tourist on the street or at a café in Gurney Drive / Pulau Tikus / Jalan Penang asking 'friendly' questions (directions, hotel recommendations, 'you are Japanese? my wife is Japanese'); (b) handshake, shoulder-touch or close-proximity conversation during which a spray, scented cloth, or rapid-speech 'trance induction' is used; (c) victim becomes compliant and walks with the scammer to an ATM, hotel room, or car, willingly handing over cash, jewellery, watches, and PIN codes; (d) victim 'wakes up' 30 minutes to several hours later with no memory and wallet/jewellery missing; (e) syndicate variant per Nov 2025 FMT raid: the 14 Japanese detainees + 4 Chinese nationals operated from two Simpang Ampat bungalows running police-impersonation phone scams targeting Japanese victims abroad. For travellers: (1) if any stranger — especially a well-dressed foreigner — approaches you with 'friendly' conversation in Gurney, Pulau Tikus, Jalan Penang or around Armenian Street, STEP BACK out of handshake / shoulder-touch range and say 'no thank you' firmly; (2) NEVER accept an offered drink, cigarette, or scented business card from a stranger — pukau operators use aerosols or treated paper; (3) do NOT walk with any stranger to an ATM, hotel, or vehicle under any circumstance — that is the canonical pukau end-state; (4) if you feel a sudden 'cloudy' or 'floaty' sensation during conversation, IMMEDIATELY walk into the nearest hotel lobby, 7-Eleven or restaurant and sit until it passes (10–30 min); (5) solo older travellers are the primary target — walk in pairs at dusk in Gurney Drive and Pulau Tikus especially; (6) keep passport + cards in hotel safe; carry one card + RM 200 cash max; (7) if robbed, call 999 immediately and file report at George Town police HQ — the 2025 syndicate was broken precisely because tourists filed reports; (8) Tourism Malaysia 24-hr tourist line 1-300-88-5050 (English).
scams.avoidance: Step back from handshake range of any 'friendly' stranger in Gurney, Pulau Tikus, Armenian St NEVER accept drink, cigarette, scented card from a stranger — pukau uses aerosols Do NOT walk with any stranger to an ATM, hotel, or vehicle — canonical pukau end-state If you feel 'cloudy' mid-conversation, immediately enter a hotel lobby or 7-Eleven Solo older travellers primary target — walk in pairs at dusk; call 999; Tourism Malaysia 1-300-88-5050
scams.location: Persiaran Gurney / Gurney Drive seafront promenade, Gurney Plaza entrances, Pulau Tikus shophouses, Jalan Penang hotel strip, Upper Penang Road bar district, Armenian Street / Love Lane café zone, George Town Eastern & Oriental / Cheong Fatt Tze heritage hotel forecourts

scams.name: Penang International Airport (PEN) Grab Cancellation & Taxi-Tout Scam
scams.description: Penang International Airport (PEN) in Bayan Lepas is Penang's most-documented 2024–2025 tourist-transport friction point, where the airport taxi mafia, Grab driver cancellations, and 'prebet sapu' (unlicensed) touts converge. Community reports from 2024–2025 document the prepaid-taxi-vs-Grab calculation and late-night arrival pain ('I arrived at the airport at 11pm and wasn't able to call a grab'). A July 10 2025 law change made unauthorised taxi touting explicitly illegal at PEN, but enforcement is uneven. The 2025 scams: (a) Grab driver accepts your PEN airport pickup then cancels 2–3 minutes before arrival, repeating the cancellation 3–4 times until you give up and walk to the taxi queue; (b) PEN taxi mafia — drivers at the 'authorised' taxi counter quote RM 80–RM 120 to George Town (15 km) when real Grab rate is RM 25–RM 45; prepaid taxi coupons inside arrivals are RM 44.70 to George Town, RM 74.30 to Batu Ferringhi (legitimate rates, but many drivers demand cash 'surcharge' on top); (c) 'prebet sapu' unlicensed drivers approach with 'taxi? Taxi? Good price' in arrivals — 100% scam, no insurance, no recourse; (d) short-ride refusals — if your destination is 5–8 km the taxi queue driver refuses or demands RM 60+ minimum; (e) late-night (11 PM–5 AM) Grab coverage is thin — the only real driver pickup zone is level 1 outside arrivals, and touts exploit this gap. For travellers: (1) book Grab or InDrive BEFORE walking out — use airport Wi-Fi, meet driver at the signposted Grab pickup zone level 1 outside arrivals; the real rate to George Town is RM 25–RM 45; (2) if driver cancels, accept it, cancel on your side too (no fee) and rebook — do NOT WhatsApp drivers or accept 'cash off-app' deals; (3) for pre-booked reliability use Grab 'Advance Booking' 24 hours ahead; (4) if Grab is unavailable (late-night arrivals), use the OFFICIAL prepaid taxi coupon desk inside arrivals — RM 44.70 George Town / RM 74.30 Batu Ferringhi — pay at the desk, NOT to the driver, and keep the coupon as receipt; (5) NEVER accept any 'taxi? taxi?' offer from someone approaching you inside arrivals — these are 'prebet sapu' unlicensed touts now criminalised since July 10 2025; (6) Rapid Penang bus 401E goes from PEN to KOMTAR for RM 3.40 (45 min, 6 AM–11 PM); (7) keep luggage between your feet at the Grab pickup zone — bag-snatching from taxi queues is rare but documented; (8) save Grab support in-app and PDRM 999 for any serious dispute.
scams.avoidance: Book Grab/InDrive BEFORE leaving arrivals — meet at signposted level 1 pickup zone If driver cancels, cancel your side too (no fee) and rebook — no WhatsApp, no off-app If no Grab (late-night), use OFFICIAL prepaid taxi coupon desk INSIDE arrivals — pay the desk NEVER accept 'taxi? taxi?' from anyone approaching inside arrivals — illegal since Jul 10 2025 Rapid Penang 401E to KOMTAR is RM 3.40 (45 min); Grab Advance Booking 24 hrs ahead
scams.location: Penang International Airport (PEN) Bayan Lepas arrivals hall, prepaid taxi coupon desk, Grab pickup zone level 1, PEN departure curb, airport-taxi queue outside arrivals, Rapid Penang 401E bus stop

scams.name: Gurney Drive & New Lane Hawker 'Tourist Price' Overcharge
scams.description: Penang's famed hawker culture has a documented 'tourist price' overlay at specific centres — Gurney Drive Hawker Centre, New Lane (Macalister Road), and parts of Chulia Street — where unlabelled prices and 'seafood market rate' ambushes inflate bills 2–5x local norms. Community warnings are blunt ('AVOID GURNEY DRIVE HAWKER it's a total tourist trap') and travelers note 'very very overpriced' at tourist hawker nodes. The broader 'unlabelled hawker stall' pattern recurs across Malaysian tourist zones. TripSavvy and Yelp tourist reviews of Gurney Drive independently confirm 'overcharging tourists, particularly at night.' The 2025 overcharge patterns: (a) seafood stalls at Gurney Drive and New Lane quoting 'market price' with no menu — grilled stingray, prawn mee, cockles billed at RM 60–RM 150 per dish when local rate is RM 20–RM 40; (b) char koay teow charged RM 18–RM 25 at Gurney tourist stalls vs RM 8–RM 12 at local kopitiam; (c) 'fresh coconut' or 'fresh sugarcane juice' RM 15–RM 20 vs RM 4–RM 6 local; (d) menu without prices, bill arrives only after food consumed, dispute creates 'lose face' pressure; (e) 'tourist English menu' vs 'Malay/Chinese menu' price discrimination at a minority of stalls; (f) extra-charge for condiments (sambal, belacan, pickles) that are free for locals. For travellers: (1) AVOID Gurney Drive Hawker Centre for first-time Penang food — community consensus calls it 'a total tourist trap'; go to Chulia Street night stalls, Kimberley Street, Lorong Selamat or Sri Weld food court instead; (2) ALWAYS ask 'berapa?' (how much) BEFORE ordering — a stall that hesitates or refuses to quote is the red flag; (3) NEVER order 'seafood market price' without a written quote — ask the stall owner to write the per-kg or per-piece price on a napkin; (4) local benchmark prices (2025–2026): char koay teow RM 8–RM 12, hokkien mee RM 8–RM 12, laksa RM 7–RM 10, nasi kandar RM 10–RM 18, fresh juice RM 4–RM 6, teh tarik RM 2.50–RM 4; (5) pay with exact change when possible — 'no change' is a minor shakedown; (6) if overcharged, stay calm, pay only what you agreed, photograph the stall and file a complaint with MBPP (Majlis Bandaraya Pulau Pinang) municipal council 04-263-7637; (7) Gurney Drive Hawker Centre is currently relocated to 'Gurney Bay' — confirm address before travel; (8) TouchNGo eWallet or DuitNow QR is accepted at many stalls and auto-logs receipts for disputes.
scams.avoidance: AVOID Gurney Drive Hawker Centre first time — go Chulia St, Kimberley St, Lorong Selamat ALWAYS ask 'berapa?' BEFORE ordering — refusal to quote is the red flag NEVER order 'seafood market price' without a written per-kg quote on paper Benchmark: char koay teow RM 8–RM 12, laksa RM 7–RM 10, fresh juice RM 4–RM 6 Pay with exact change; file complaint with MBPP 04-263-7637 if overcharged
scams.location: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre / Gurney Bay relocation site, Persiaran Gurney seafront, New Lane (Lorong Baru) Macalister Road night stalls, Lorong Selamat, Chulia Street backpacker strip, Komtar food-court ring, Love Lane café zone

scams.name: George Town Street-Art & Costumed-Character Photo Shakedown
scams.description: George Town's Ernest Zacharevic street-art murals (Armenian Street, Lebuh Ah Quee, Cannon Street, Lebuh Muntri) and Upper Penang Road / Love Lane nightlife zone host a 2024–2025 'photo shakedown' ecosystem where a 'friendly local' offers to take a tourist's photo, poses in costume, or produces an on-the-spot 'caricature' then demands RM 50–RM 500 afterwards. Community reports document the 'sob-story / stranger approach' pattern with photo/selfie variants and the broader Malaysia-wide tourist scam landscape. theSun / Instagram viral content from September 2025 documented the KLCC / Penang 'photo taken by friendly local then RM 100–RM 500 charged' pattern. 'Penang Travel Safety Tips: The Sifu Scam' (wanderingdejavu.com) documents a closely-related street-art shakedown where a self-proclaimed 'sifu / fortune teller' approaches tourists at George Town murals offering 'free' palm reading or photo then demands payment. The 2025 tactics: (a) around 'Little Children on a Bicycle' (Armenian Street) and 'Boy on Chair' (Cannon Street) murals, a person waits with a camera or phone offering 'I take your photo with mural, my angle better!' — afterwards demands RM 50–RM 200 'photo service fee'; (b) costumed characters (cartoon mascots, Spider-Man, Pikachu) on Upper Penang Road and Love Lane pose in photos then demand RM 50 per photo / per family member; (c) 'free caricature' artists at Armenian Street draw first then demand RM 200; (d) 'photo permission' touts at murals claiming the mural 'requires a photo fee' of RM 20–RM 50 (100% fake — all Zacharevic murals are free public art); (e) 'fortune teller / sifu' approach near Kuan Yin Temple or Goddess of Mercy Temple offering 'free' reading then demanding RM 100–RM 500; (f) night variant on Upper Penang Road: a 'local guide' offers to 'show you the best bars for free', delivers you to a scam bar with RM 800+ final tab. For travellers: (1) all Ernest Zacharevic street murals in George Town are FREE public art — NO ONE has authority to charge a 'photo fee' or 'photo permission'; (2) if a stranger offers to take your photo, politely say 'no thanks, my friend will' — hand your phone only to fellow travellers or hotel staff; (3) if a costumed character approaches, do NOT pose — keep walking; photographing them from 3m+ without posing is free; (4) 'free' caricature, 'free' photo, 'free' palm-reading, 'free' bar guide = always a shakedown — refuse at 'free'; (5) if pressured for payment after an unrequested service, offer RM 5–RM 10 max and walk firmly — these scammers rarely escalate if you don't engage verbally; (6) the 2025 shakedown targets solo foreign tourists, especially older travellers with visible cameras / phones — keep your phone in your bag between shots; (7) if threatened or surrounded, walk to the nearest café (Mugshot Coffee, ChinaHouse, Narrow Marrow) and ask them to call PDRM 999; (8) George Town Tourist Information Centre at Lebuh Pantai is the reliable source for legitimate paid tours.
scams.avoidance: ALL Ernest Zacharevic murals are FREE public art — no 'photo fee' is legitimate If a stranger offers to take your photo: 'no thanks' — phone only to fellow travellers 'Free' caricature, photo, palm-reading, bar-guide = always a shakedown — refuse at 'free' Offer RM 5–RM 10 max if pressured after unrequested service, walk firmly Solo tourists are primary target — phone in bag between shots; PDRM 999 if threatened
scams.location: Armenian Street 'Little Children on a Bicycle' mural, Cannon Street 'Boy on Chair' mural, Lebuh Ah Quee, Lebuh Muntri, Love Lane café strip, Upper Penang Road bar district, Kuan Yin Temple forecourt, Clan Jetties (Chew / Lee / Tan Jetty) tourist entrances

scams.name: George Town Trishaw Tour Bait-and-Switch & Commission Stops
scams.description: Penang's trishaws (beca) are a genuine George Town heritage institution and mostly operate fairly, but a persistent 2024–2025 bait-and-switch targets foreign tourists at KOMTAR, Cheong Fatt Tze 'Blue Mansion', Armenian Street, Swettenham Pier (cruise days), and Penang Ferry Terminal. A viral 2025 incident — a China tourist tearing up cash notes in a heated argument with a Penang trishaw rider — confirmed the fare-dispute pattern. Community reports also confirm trishaw touts waiting at Swettenham Pier for cruise passengers. The 2025 tactics: (a) driver quotes 'RM 40 for 1-hour heritage tour' then after 15 minutes diverts to commission-paying batik shops, souvenir stalls, 'famous' herbal medicine stores, or a 'ancestral temple' with donation pressure — each stop 10–20 min; (b) promised landmarks (Blue Mansion, Clan Jetties, street-art murals) 'skipped due to traffic / road closure'; (c) end-of-ride 'surprise' — driver claims 'RM 40 per person' (not total), or 'one hour' was '45 minutes' and demands RM 60 'extra'; (d) Swettenham Pier cruise-day variant — trishaw tout promises '1-hour city tour return to ship' at RM 50, returns you late to miss boarding deadline unless tip paid; (e) post-midnight fare-gouging on Chulia Street / Love Lane for bar-to-hotel rides — RM 50 for a 5-minute ride; (f) some drivers refuse the agreed price and demand 'RM 100 tip for tourist' at drop-off, with aggressive standover tactics per the viral 2025 incident video. For travellers: (1) a fair 2025 George Town trishaw heritage tour is RM 40–RM 60 per HOUR per trishaw (1–2 passengers) — confirm per-hour vs per-person IN WRITING before boarding; (2) name specific landmarks you want to see ('Blue Mansion — Clan Jetties — Armenian Street murals — back to KOMTAR') and refuse all unrequested shop stops; (3) snap a photo of the trishaw licence plate / driver ID before departing as insurance; (4) pay in cash at the END of the agreed tour, not partway; carry RM 60 in RM 10 notes for exact change; (5) for cruise-day tours from Swettenham Pier, agree return deadline with 45-min buffer before boarding close; (6) honestly, the George Town heritage zone is 100% walkable in 2 hours — the free George Town Heritage Trail map (from Tourist Information Centre at Lebuh Pantai) covers all UNESCO sites without any trishaw; (7) if overcharged at drop-off, DO NOT escalate — pay the agreed amount, leave, and report the trishaw plate + driver to MBPP Tourism Council 04-263-7637 or Tourism Malaysia 1-300-88-5050; (8) avoid Upper Penang Road and Chulia Street trishaw hire after 10 PM — late-night fares are persistently gouged.
scams.avoidance: Fair rate: RM 40–RM 60 per HOUR per trishaw (1–2 passengers) — not per person Confirm per-hour vs per-person IN WRITING; name specific landmarks; refuse shop stops Photograph licence plate / driver ID before boarding; pay at END in cash exact change Cruise-day tours from Swettenham Pier: agree return with 45-min buffer before boarding Heritage zone is 100% walkable — use free Tourist Info map from Lebuh Pantai instead
scams.location: KOMTAR trishaw stand, Cheong Fatt Tze 'Blue Mansion' forecourt, Armenian Street murals, Clan Jetties entrance, Swettenham Pier cruise terminal, Penang Ferry Terminal (Butterworth), Chulia Street / Love Lane night hire, Upper Penang Road post-midnight

scams.name: George Town Tourist Minimart Unlabelled-Price Overcharge
scams.description: George Town's heritage core around Armenian Street, Chulia Street, Love Lane, Lebuh Muntri, and the Clan Jetties entrances hosts a 2024–2025 'tourist minimart' overcharge ecosystem where independent shops (not the 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, KK Mart chains) keep products unpriced and ring up 2–5x the real rate on bottled water, snacks, sunscreen, SIM cards, and souvenirs. Community reports confirm the tourist-price overlays persist, including at transport hubs like Penang Sentral. The 2025 tactics: (a) 1.5 L bottle of mineral water rung at RM 6–RM 10 vs RM 2 at 7-Eleven; (b) small pack of tissues RM 8 vs RM 1 local; (c) prepaid SIM-card shops on Chulia Street quoting RM 80 for RM 35 Celcom/DiGi tourist SIM; (d) no price labels on shelves, cashier rings up quickly during conversational distraction ('where from? first time Penang?'); (e) souvenir keychain / fridge-magnet RM 25 at Armenian Street tourist shops vs RM 5 at Chowrasta Market; (f) sunscreen, mosquito repellent, Panadol, Pocari Sweat — all 2–3x real Watsons / Guardian pharmacy prices; (g) Clan Jetties entrance shops selling 'durian cake' and 'Penang souvenirs' at 3x real bakery / Him Heang / Ghee Hiang prices; (h) Love Lane / Lebuh Muntri 'convenience store' charging RM 15 for a beer that is RM 6 at 7-Eleven 100m away. For travellers: (1) always shop at CHAIN stores — 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, KK Mart, Watsons, Guardian — for water, snacks, pharmacy, SIM; prices are labelled and fixed; (2) benchmark 2025–2026 prices: 1.5 L water RM 1.80–RM 2.50, 600 ml water RM 1.20, can of beer RM 5–RM 8, Panadol 10-pack RM 4–RM 6, Celcom/DiGi tourist SIM RM 30–RM 40; (3) ALWAYS ask 'berapa?' (how much) for each item BEFORE placing it on the counter at any independent shop — cashier refusal or vague 'we calculate later' is the red flag; (4) for souvenirs, buy at Chowrasta Market (heritage wet market, Jalan Penang) or Him Heang / Ghee Hiang / Sim Huat biscuit shops — 50–70% cheaper than Armenian Street tourist stalls; (5) for SIM cards, go directly to Celcom / DiGi / Maxis branded stores at Gurney Plaza, Queensbay Mall, or PEN airport arrivals — NEVER buy from Chulia Street independent booths; (6) always request a receipt — scam shops often refuse; (7) pay by TouchNGo eWallet or DuitNow QR when possible — auto-receipt and dispute trail; (8) if overcharged, calmly pay, photograph the shop, and report to Malaysian Consumer Tribunal (Tribunal Tuntutan Pengguna Malaysia, TTPM) at ttpm.kpdnhep.gov.my — recoveries under RM 50,000 are possible for tourists.
scams.avoidance: Shop at CHAIN stores only — 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, KK Mart, Watsons, Guardian Benchmark: 1.5 L water RM 1.80–RM 2.50, beer RM 5–RM 8, DiGi SIM RM 30–RM 40 ALWAYS ask 'berapa?' per item BEFORE counter at independent shops — vague reply = red flag Souvenirs: Chowrasta Market, Him Heang, Ghee Hiang — 50–70% cheaper than Armenian St Pay by TouchNGo / DuitNow QR for auto-receipt; report to TTPM if overcharged
scams.location: Armenian Street independent shops, Chulia Street backpacker-strip minimarts, Love Lane / Lebuh Muntri convenience stores, Clan Jetties (Chew / Lee / Tan Jetty) entrance souvenir shops, Lebuh Ah Quee mural-adjacent kiosks, Little India souvenir stalls, Swettenham Pier cruise-terminal gift shops
